title: sre weekly ops sync prep - 2026-03-31 (draft)
body:
Prep notes for SRE weekly ops sync (Wed 2026-03-31) - draft

Attendees (prep): Jordan, Alex, Ethan, Samira (lead)
Meeting goal: quick review of SLO health, paging trends, recent sev incidents, and unblock rollout of new paging policy. Keep to 45m.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: Quick wins / housekeeping (on-call rotation change, runbook updates)
- 10m: SLO review (prod web + inference runtime)
- 10m: Paging trends and noise sources (alerts to quiet)
- 5m: Top incidents post-mortem highlights (actions only)
- 5m: Action items & owners + follow-ups

SLOs (current snapshots)
- prod-web availability (p90-region): target 99.95% monthly; current month-to-date 99.86% (gap ~0.09%).
  - Major contributor: 2026-03-18 traffic spike causing autoscale lag in us-west (see incident below)
- inference-runtime latency (p99 token-gen): target 200ms; MTD 230ms (outside target).
  - Contributing: increased batched requests for long sequences in dedicated pools; also new kernel deployment 2026-03-24 shows +15ms p99.
- embeddings service error rate: target <0.1%; MTD 0.07% (OK)

Paging trends (last 30d):
- Total pages per week: avg 62 -> down from 78 two weeks ago. Improvement after alert tuning on 2026-03-10.
- Noise sources: 40% of pages are from memory-pressure alerts on legacy dedicated pools (we've suppressed some noisy alerts but need longer-term fix).
- Alert fatigue: avg pager acknowledgement time still ~9m on weekends. Need clearer weekend escalation path.

Top incidents to highlight (post-mortem quick notes):
1) 2026-03-18 - autoscale lag causing 4% error spike on prod-web (sev2)
   - Summary: sudden +3x traffic from partner batch job; HPA metrics lagged due to custom metric TTL. Autoscaler scaled only after 6 minutes -> latency +5s for some endpoints.
   - Mitigations in place: reduced metric TTL to 30s, added warm standby for partner namespace, dashboard alert for HPA underserve.
   - Actions: Alex -> add playbook for partner burst (owner: Alex, due: 2026-04-07)

2) 2026-03-24 - kernel rollout increased p99 latency for inference-runtime (sev3)
   - Summary: new attention kernel compiled for ~A100 produced regression at long sequences; affected dedicated pools with quantized model variants.
   - Rollback: rolled back to previous kernel in 20m, mitigation: pin kernel per model family while we debug.
   - Actions: Jordan + Research -> reproduce regression on staging with long-seq test set (owner: Jordan, due: 2026-04-02)

3) 2026-03-26 - noisy memory-pressure alerts (sev3)
   - Summary: memory fragmentation on older driver versions in dedicated pools triggered alerts; pages were largely informational.
   - Short-term: suppressed non-critical alert thresholds, scheduled drivers upgrade.
   - Actions: Ethan -> schedule upgrade for legacy pools (owner: Ethan, due: 2026-04-09)

Runbooks & playbooks status
- prod-web autoscale playbook: draft v0.2 (needs runbook steps for partner bursts) - Samira to finalize.
- inference kernel rollout playbook: v1 in repo, need to add canary measurement checklist and rollback thresholds. Jordan to update.

Open risks / discussion points for meeting
- Long-tail latency regressions when batching long sequences. We need an on-call quick test harness that can simulate long-seq batch patterns against dedicated pools. (Proposal: small periodic canary job in each pool; requires infra quotas)
- Weekend paging: consider an on-call buddy pool for weekends or a simplified escalation matrix to reduce ack time.
- Capacity: dedicated pools for enterprise customers showing higher cold-start variance; potential to offer warm standby option as paid feature.

Action items (captured for follow-up)
- Alex: Implement autoscale partner burst playbook + add HPA dashboard alert (due 2026-04-07)
- Jordan: Reproduce kernel perf regression on staging with long-seq dataset; add rollback thresholds to rollout playbook (due 2026-04-02)
- Ethan: Schedule driver upgrades for legacy dedicated pools and validate memory metrics post-upgrade (due 2026-04-09)
- Samira: Finalize prod-web autoscale playbook and coordinate on-call weekend escalation proposal (due 2026-04-05)
- All: Add one-line status updates to the shared ops Slack #sre-ops by EOD Friday

Notes to self (Samira):
- Bring concrete numbers to meeting (p99 delta pre/post kernel rollback, pages/week trendline)
- Ask product/solutions if any upcoming partner jobs scheduled that could cause another burst (ping @solutions-eng)
- Follow up with legal/privacy before scheduling any additional customer-facing warm-standby docs (if we decide to surface feature)

Links / refs: CONFLUENCE-1234 (prod-web autoscale notes), JIRA-SRE-987 (kernel regression investigation), slack thread #infra-kernels 2026-03-24

Scratchpad / things to ask during sync:
- "Do we want to treat partner bursts as predictable traffic (and bill for warm standby)?"
- "Is there appetite to add an explicit weekend on-call buddy or rotate a smaller weekend crew?"
- "Can Platform add a lightweight canary job for long-seq workloads? What's the infra cost?"

End of draft prep notes. Will iterate after feedback from Jordan/Alex/Ethan before 2026-03-31 sync.
